advances: Closes the sign split for the original three-height simplex source class: an arbitrary independent product may contain positive, zero, and negative transverse tilts simultaneously. A common row moment constant yields one absolute mean-cap bound through one application of the independent-row odd-center/even-drift/noise lemma.
author: research-agent
proof:
Work first in one original row and suppress its index. Thus \(m,h,L,\beta,\theta,j,\mathbf a,t\) denote its parameters. Write \(X_\Sigma:=\sum_{k=1}^mX_k\), \(B_y:=L-hy\), \(\mu_y:=\mathbb E[X_\Sigma\mid Y=y]\), \(v_y:=\operatorname{Var}(X_\Sigma\mid Y=y)\), and \(p_y:=\Pr(Y=y)\). These are the original conditional total, budgets, means, and variances of 43cb56218b18ec82 and bfb60080994e80cc. The letters \(R\) and \(p\) for the original source law in the predecessors both mean this row's \(R_i\).

Every original support atom has positive probability. In particular \((\mathbf e_1,0)\) is supported, so \(j=\mathbb EX_1>0\) and its integrality gives \(j\ge1\). The original slack \(L-X_\Sigma-hY\) is nonnegative and is strictly positive at the positive-probability origin. Its mean is the positive integer \(L-mj-h\), hence \(L-mj-h\ge1\). It follows that \(B_1\ge m+1\) and that \((j\mathbf1_m,1)\) is an atom in the original support.

The original height support is exactly \(\{0,1,2\}\). Its mean condition gives \(p_0=p_2\); denote their common value by \(\varepsilon\). We record its exact probabilities and the middle-mass bound for all real tilts. Use the original partition
\[
 Z_m(B,u):=\sum_{\substack{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^m\\\sum_kx_k\le B}}e^{u\sum_kx_k}
          =\sum_{s=0}^B\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}e^{us},
 \qquad Z_y:=Z_m(B_y,\beta).
\]
The equality follows by counting complete compositions of each total \(s\). For fixed real \(u\), let \(w_s=\binom{s+m-1}{m-1}e^{us}\). Its successive ratios \(w_{s+1}/w_s=e^u(s+m)/(s+1)\) are nonincreasing. Thus, for \(B\ge1\) and \(1\le s\le B\), \(w_{B+1}w_{s-1}\le w_Bw_s\). Summing proves
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 w_{B+1}Z_m(B-1,u)&\le w_B\sum_{s=1}^Bw_s<w_BZ_m(B,u),\\
 Z_m(B,u)^2-Z_m(B-1,u)Z_m(B+1,u)
 &=w_BZ_m(B,u)-w_{B+1}Z_m(B-1,u)>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the successive differences of \(\log Z_m(B,u)\) decrease. Comparing the two consecutive budget intervals of length \(h\) gives \(Z_0Z_2\le Z_1^2\), also when \(B_2=0\).

The original probabilities are proportional to \(Z_0,e^\theta Z_1,e^{2\theta}Z_2\). Equality of the endpoints yields \(e^{2\theta}Z_2=Z_0\), so they are exactly
\[
 p_0=p_2=\varepsilon
   =\frac{\sqrt{Z_0Z_2}}{Z_1+2\sqrt{Z_0Z_2}},
 \qquad p_1=1-2\varepsilon\ge\frac13.
\]
These are the original probabilities in 43cb56218b18ec82, with the same partition normalization. The involution \(y\mapsto2-y\) therefore preserves the original height law for every sign of \(\beta\).

Put \(\bar a:=m^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^ma_k\), \(\mathbf a^\perp:=\mathbf a-\bar a\mathbf1_m\), \(U:=X_\Sigma-\mu_Y\), and \(N^\perp:=\mathbf a^\perp\cdot\mathbf X\). Permutation symmetry gives \(\mathbb E[\mathbf X\mid Y=y]=(\mu_y/m)\mathbf1_m\). Conditional on \((Y,X_\Sigma)=(y,s)\), the transverse vector is uniform on all complete compositions of \(s\) into \(m\) parts, since its original weight depends only on \(y,s\). In particular \(\mathbb E[N^\perp\mid Y,X_\Sigma]=0\), including \(m=1\), where \(\mathbf a^\perp=\mathbf0\). Therefore the original noise \(N=\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf X-\mathbb E[\mathbf X\mid Y])\) satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 N&=\bar a U+N^\perp,\qquad \mathbb E[UN^\perp]=0,\\
 \sigma^2:=\mathbb EN^2
   &=\bar a^2\mathbb EU^2+\mathbb E(N^\perp)^2
     =\bar a^2\sum_{y=0}^2p_yv_y+\mathbb E(N^\perp)^2
     \ge\frac{\bar a^2v_1}{3}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

Suppose \(\beta<0\) and \(m\ge2\). The hypotheses of bfb60080994e80cc hold for precisely this original \(U\), and give \(\mathbb EU^4\le2^{101}(\mathbb EU^2)^2\). The hypotheses of 58fe9c7d09f27e78 hold for \(\mathbf b=\mathbf a^\perp\); its scalar \(N\) equals our \(N^\perp\). It gives \(\mathbb E(N^\perp)^4\le3\cdot10^9(\mathbb E(N^\perp)^2)^2\). Using \(|x+y|^4\le8(|x|^4+|y|^4)\) and the preceding orthogonal variance identity yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb EN^4
 &\le8\left[2^{101}\bar a^4(\mathbb EU^2)^2
              +3\cdot10^9(\mathbb E(N^\perp)^2)^2\right]\\
 &\le2^{104}\left[\bar a^2\mathbb EU^2+\mathbb E(N^\perp)^2\right]^2
   =2^{104}\sigma^4.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(3\cdot10^9<2^{101}\). If \(\beta<0\) and \(m=1\), the scalar noise in 844fb74d3b46622a is our \(U\), and \(N=a_1U\). Scaling its bound gives \(\mathbb EN^4\le2^{35}\sigma^4\). If \(\beta\ge0\), 9ba4a3963a51edd3 applies directly to the original \(N\), including \(m=1\) and \(\beta=0\), and gives \(\mathbb EN^4\le3\cdot10^{11}\sigma^4\). These cases establish \(\mathbb EN^4\le K\sigma^4\) for every real tilt with the single common choice \(K:=2^{104}\). All scaling and variance inequalities include zero directions without division.

Now set \(Y^\circ:=Y-1\) and \(\Omega:=\mu_0+\mu_2-2\mu_1\), with exactly the original-source meaning of \(\Omega\) in 43cb56218b18ec82. Interpolation at the three original heights and averaging with their original probabilities give
\[
 \mu_Y=\mu_1+\frac{\mu_2-\mu_0}{2}Y^\circ
                 +\frac{\Omega}{2}(Y^\circ)^2,
 \qquad mj=\mu_1+\varepsilon\Omega.
\]
Define the scalar variables for b0f9a49859be646c by
\[
 W:=\left(t+\bar a\frac{\mu_2-\mu_0}{2}\right)Y^\circ,
 \qquad
 V:=\frac{\bar a\Omega}{2}\bigl((Y^\circ)^2-2\varepsilon\bigr).
\]
Their latent element is the original \(Y\), and their noise is the original \(N\) already defined. The interpolation gives the pointwise identity \(\mathbf a\cdot(\mathbf X-j\mathbf1_m)+t(Y-1)=W+V+N\). Under the measure-preserving involution \(y\mapsto2-y\), \(W\) is odd and \(V\) is even. Moreover \(\mathbb EV=0\), since \(\mathbb E(Y^\circ)^2=2\varepsilon\), and \(\mathbb E[N\mid Y]=0\).

If \(\beta\ne0\), 43cb56218b18ec82 applies to this original law for either sign and gives \(\varepsilon\Omega^4\le2^{36}v_1^2\). The variable \((Y^\circ)^2\) is Bernoulli with its original parameter \(q=2\varepsilon\). Its centered fourth moment equals \(q(1-q)^4+(1-q)q^4=q(1-q)((1-q)^3+q^3)\le q\). Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb EV^4
 &\le\frac{\bar a^4\Omega^4}{16}\,2\varepsilon
   \le2^{33}\bar a^4v_1^2
   \le9\cdot2^{33}\sigma^4
   \le K\sigma^4.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The last comparison follows from \(9<2^{71}\), and no step divides by \(\bar a\) or \(\sigma\).

If \(\beta=0\), the conditional transverse law at budget \(B_y\) is uniform on its complete budget simplex. Appending its slack \(B_y-X_\Sigma\) gives a bijection with the uniform complete compositions of \(B_y\) into \(m+1\) parts. Permutation symmetry of those parts gives \(\mu_y=mB_y/(m+1)=m(L-hy)/(m+1)\), including \(B_y=0\). This is affine in \(y\), so \(\Omega=V=0\). The same drift fourth-moment bound follows directly in this case.

Restore all row indices, producing \(W_i,V_i,N_i\) and \(\sigma_i^2=\mathbb EN_i^2\). For every row the original height involution makes \(W_i\) odd and \(V_i\) even, and we have \(\mathbb EV_i=0\), \(\mathbb E[N_i\mid Y_i]=0\), \(\mathbb EN_i^4\le K\sigma_i^4\), and \(\mathbb EV_i^4\le K\sigma_i^4\), with the same \(K=2^{104}\ge1\). The full experiments \((Y_i,N_i)\) are independent because they are measurable functions of the independent original rows. The original centered projection is pointwise \(T=\sum_i(W_i+V_i+N_i)\). Apply the independent-row sum extension of b0f9a49859be646c once to these exact original row experiments. It gives both cap probabilities at least \(1/(196608K)=c\), and gives the stronger lower bound \(1/2\) when \(\sum_i\sigma_i^2=0\). This application includes products whose rows have different signs of tilt.

The earlier slack calculation shows that every row's full mean is in its original lattice support, so \(\bar{\mathbf z}\) belongs to their product. If a closed halfspace \(H=\{\mathbf z:\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf z\ge u\}\) contains \(\bar{\mathbf z}\), then \(u\le\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\bar{\mathbf z}\). Thus \(H\) contains the event \(\{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot(\mathbf z-\bar{\mathbf z})\ge0\}\). Splitting \(\boldsymbol\ell\) into the original row coefficients makes the latter event precisely \(\{T\ge0\}\), which has original product probability at least \(c\). A zero projection is identically zero and has both cap probabilities one. Every support, mean, conditional law, and probability used above remains the originally specified one, including all zero upper budgets.
statement:
Let \(b\ge1\) be an integer. For each \(1\le i\le b\), let \(m_i,h_i,L_i\ge1\) be integers with \(2h_i\le L_i<3h_i\), and let \(\beta_i,\theta_i\in\mathbb R\) be finite. Let the full row experiments \((\mathbf X^{(i)},Y_i)\) be independent and have the original laws
\[
 R_i(\mathbf x,y)=\frac{\exp(\beta_i\sum_{k=1}^{m_i}x_k+\theta_i y)}{\mathcal Z_i},
 \qquad
 (\mathbf x,y)\in E_{L_i,h_i,m_i}
 :=\left\{(\mathbf x,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m_i+1}:
            \sum_{k=1}^{m_i}x_k+h_i y\le L_i\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal Z_i\) is the original normalizing constant. Suppose \(\mathbb E(\mathbf X^{(i)},Y_i)=(j_i\mathbf1_{m_i},1)\), with integer \(j_i\). For arbitrary \(\mathbf a^{(i)}\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\) and \(t_i\in\mathbb R\), put
\[
 T:=\sum_{i=1}^b\left[
       \mathbf a^{(i)}\cdot(\mathbf X^{(i)}-j_i\mathbf1_{m_i})
          +t_i(Y_i-1)\right],
 \qquad
 c:=\frac1{196608\cdot2^{104}}=\frac1{3\cdot2^{120}}.
\]
Then \(\min\{\Pr(T\ge0),\Pr(T\le0)\}\ge c\), under the original product law. The full mean \(\bar{\mathbf z}:=((j_i\mathbf1_{m_i},1))_{i=1}^b\) belongs to the product of the original lattice supports, and every closed halfspace containing \(\bar{\mathbf z}\) has original product probability at least \(c\).

Define the original conditional transverse noise by \(N_i:=\mathbf a^{(i)}\cdot(\mathbf X^{(i)}-\mathbb E[\mathbf X^{(i)}\mid Y_i])\), and set \(\sigma_i^2:=\mathbb EN_i^2\). If \(\sum_i\sigma_i^2=0\), both displayed projection probabilities are at least \(1/2\). The statement includes \(m_i=1\), \(L_i=2h_i\), \(\beta_i=0\), and zero projection directions. The constant is independent of all original parameters, of the number of rows, and of all directions.
